Kathmandu, August 24

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has become the fifth-highest-grossing foreign film in Nepal. By Monday afternoon, the film had crossed Rs 160 million at the domestic box office.

The film’s total gross collection so far stands at Rs 160.2 million.

It is projected to overtake the Indian film Animal, starring Ranbir Kapoor, which has grossed a total of Rs 165.6 million, by this coming weekend.

Interestingly, “Spider-Man” is the only Hollywood film to feature in Nepal’s top 10 highest-grossing foreign films list.

title: Nepals first modern tunnel road at Nagdhunga opens to public on trial basis - Daily Excelsior
description: Nepals first modern tunnel road at Nagdhunga opens to public on trial basis  Daily Excelsior
publisher.title: Daily Excelsior
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Aug 24: Nepal's first modern road tunnel, the Nagdhunga passage, connecting Kathmandu to other districts, was opened to the public on Monday, allowing small private vehicles to use the tunnel road on a trial basis.

Cars, jeeps, vans and other light private vehicles carrying up to nine passengers have been allowed to use the tunnel, which was previously limited to emergency services only, said Kabiraj Shrestha, deputy chief of the Nagdhunga Tunnel Road Safety Unit.

Inaugurated on July 27, the 2.688-kilometre tunnel road was built with financial and technical assistance from the Japanese government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency.

Shreshta said the tunnel, situated in the western part of Kathmandu, will operate from 9 am to 6 pm. He added that the public won't be charged during the trial phase.

Officials have introduced strict traffic rules inside the tunnel, with speed limits capped at 40 kilometres per hour, requiring headlights on, disallowing overtaking, and prohibiting stopping or parking.

Other vehicle categories would be gradually allowed after reviewing the initial phase of operation, they added.

"We have started operations on a trial basis. A decision for its full operation will be taken after analysing the situation and collecting feedback from drivers regarding the difficulties and experiences they face while driving through the tunnel," Shrestha said.

He said the safety unit and toll collection team are preparing for a full-scale operation and are actively monitoring activities inside the tunnel through CCTV systems.

The tunnel construction officially began in October 2019, taking about seven years to complete the project. It was built at a cost of around Nepalese Rs 29 billion.

Japan provided Nepalese Rs 21.5 billion in assistance, including a loan of Nepalese Rs 5 billion, with the remaining provided by the Nepal government.

The Nagdhunga Tunnel Road, connecting Sisnekhola in Dhading district with Tutipakha, is expected to significantly reduce travel time by providing an alternative route through the busy Nagdhunga section, where traffic congestion and difficult road conditions have frequently affected movement between Kathmandu and the western districts. title: Nepali Congress Chief Whip Meets Australian Ambassador - Ratopati
description: Nepali Congress Chief Whip Meets Australian Ambassador  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. A courtesy call was held between the Chief Whip of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, Basana Thapa, and the Australian Ambassador to Nepal, Simon Anstis. In the meeting held at the Nepali Congress Parliamentary Party office on Monday, discussions were held on Nepal-Australia relations, parliamentary cooperation, education, people-to-people relations, and matters of mutual interest.

In the meeting, Chief Whip Thapa stated that parliamentary-level cooperation should be prioritized to further strengthen the relations between Nepal and Australia. She emphasized the need to increase regular dialogue and experience sharing between the parliamentarians of both countries.

Thapa said that the Nepal-Australia Parliamentary Friendship Group should be effectively mobilized to expand institutional relations between the parliamentarians of the two countries. She stated that the Parliamentary Friendship Group can be an important medium for increasing cooperation and mutual understanding on issues of common interest.

On that occasion, she praised Australia's long-standing support for Nepal's social and economic development. In particular, she expressed gratitude for Australia's contribution to Nepal's human resource development through Australia Awards Scholarships, capacity building, and training opportunities.

Thapa mentioned that Australia is a major destination for Nepali students for higher education and stated that students studying in Australia and the Nepali community living there are playing an important role in further strengthening the relations between the two countries.

In the meeting, Thapa conveyed warm greetings and best wishes to the Speaker of the Australian House of Representatives, Milton Dick, through Ambassador Anstis.

In the meeting, Ambassador Anstis said that parliamentary cooperation and people-to-people relations are important for further strengthening Nepal-Australia relations. He expressed a commitment to provide continuous support from Australia's side to further expand cooperation in areas including education, human resource development, and parliamentary cooperation in the coming days.

title: Skywell Electric Vehicles Launched in Nepal - Ratopati
description: Skywell Electric Vehicles Launched in Nepal  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Luxury Chinese electric vehicle brand 'Skywell' has entered Nepal. LRR Motors has brought the BE11 model electric vehicles of Skywell to Nepal.

According to the company, two variants of BE11 have been brought to Nepal. Both these variants will be formally unveiled on the first day of Nada Auto Show 2026, Bhadra 9. On Monday, the Vice President of the manufacturing company Skywell unveiled the Skywell logo in the presence of LRR Motors representatives, employees, and automobile enthusiasts.

According to the company, the BE11 with a 71.98 kWh capacity NMC battery pack will provide a range of up to 520 kilometers on a single full charge. Similarly, the company claims that the BE11, available with a 51.91 kWh capacity LFP battery option, will provide a range of up to 410 kilometers on a single charge.

The company stated that these EVs will be charged up to 70 percent in 35 minutes when charged with a DC fast charger. Both variants are equipped with a 150 kW capacity motor. It has an 800-volt high-voltage architecture, which supports fast charging.

The company stated that the BE11 features a panoramic sunroof, 360-degree camera, ventilated seats, ample space, and a modern body design. It has a ground clearance of 198 millimeters. The company claims that due to the high ground clearance, it can be easily driven on roads with geographical conditions like Nepal.

The price and warranty of this 5-seater EV will be informed when formally announced, the company said. According to the company, the BE11 will be launched in the market at an aggressive price. LRR Motors' stall at the Nada Auto Show is 'H19'.

title: Three killed after school bus, auto-rickshaw collide in east Nepal - Apa.az
description: Three killed after school bus, auto-rickshaw collide in east Nepal  Apa.az
publisher.title: Apa.az
full_article:
Three people were killed and two others injured after a school bus and an auto-rickshaw collided in eastern Nepal's Udayapur district on Monday morning, police said, Xinhua reports.

All five people aboard the auto-rickshaw, including its driver, were injured in the accident. "Two of the injured were pronounced dead immediately after they were taken to a hospital, while the driver died during treatment," Ganesh Bahadur Bam, the spokesperson for the district police, told Xinhua.

A preliminary police investigation suggested that the auto-rickshaw, travelling at high speed, collided with the bus, he said, adding that a detailed investigation is underway.

Police have taken the school bus driver into custody for further investigation.

title: Harka questions whether Nepal’s laws are weak or those enforcing them - Khabarhub
description: Harka questions whether Nepal’s laws are weak or those enforcing them  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Shram Sanskriti Party Chair Harkaraj Sampang has questioned whether Nepal’s laws are weak or the people responsible for enforcing them are incapable.

Speaking during the special session of the House of Representatives on Monday, Sampang questioned the effectiveness of Nepal’s legal system.

“Is our country’s law weak, or are the people enforcing the law?” Sampang asked. Comparing the situation to a vehicle, he questioned whether the problem lies with the vehicle itself or with the person unable to drive it properly.

Sampang also expressed anger over the government’s inability to bring home the bodies of Nepali migrant workers who die abroad.

He said Nepal had even been unable to recover money allegedly kept in Swiss banks, while families of Nepali migrant workers faced difficulties bringing the bodies of their loved ones back home.

Sampang said criminals were walking around as if they carried the law in their pockets, stressing that people must have fear and respect for the law.

He also called for severe punishment for those convicted of rape and murder of minor girls.

“Minor girls are being raped and murdered. Once a person is proven to be a rapist, they should be punished severely,” Sampang said.

title: Nepal imports US$158.25 million in agricultural products via Kakarbhitta - Hortidaily
description: Nepal imports US$158.25 million in agricultural products via Kakarbhitta  Hortidaily
publisher.title: Hortidaily
full_article:
Nepal imported agricultural products worth Rs 24.2674 billion (US$158.25 million) through the eastern border crossing at Kakarbhitta during fiscal year 2025/26, according to Nand Kishor Singh, chief of the Plant Quarantine Office in Kakarbhitta. The imports came from India, China, Australia, and Bangladesh, and covered food, fresh vegetables, and fruits. Singh says food grains and pulses accounted for the largest share of the total.

In the fresh vegetable category, tomatoes, cucumbers, bell peppers, and pumpkins were the main commodities imported from India. Tomatoes alone accounted for Rs 143.966 million (US$938,831), cucumbers for Rs 79.064 million (US$515,592), and chillies for Rs 32.435 million (US$211,515) over the course of the year.

Apples, pineapples, watermelons, and pears were the primary fruits imported, sourced mainly from India and China. The Plant Quarantine Office records show apples worth Rs 295.972 million (US$1.93 million) were brought in from India and China combined, while watermelons worth Rs 142.481 million (US$929,147) were imported from India.
